Subject: Payback metrics & pricing qualification for CareStream — next steps

Hi Samantha — great conversation today, appreciate you walking through the usage profile. Quick recap and a few asks so we can produce a short unit-econ packet and pilot proposal: 

Summary from call:
- Primary feature: real-time transcription + summarization for remote diagnostics (mobile devices).
- Expected initial rollout: 50k active devices (North America), target first 6 months.
- Typical session: 3 features/actions per device per day (estimating usage ramp).
- Avg tokens per feature call: ~120 tokens (you mentioned 100–150).

Asks / clarifying items we need to finalize unit economics:
1) Can you confirm the target monthly active devices and whether 50k is conservative or expected first-month?
2) Do you expect any large batch/async workloads (bulk ingest) separate from the real-time path?
3) Target commercial range: you mentioned a target spend band — can you confirm a preferred $/1M tokens target or monthly budget range to optimize a pricing structure?

What we’ll deliver next (by Tue EOD):
- Back-of-envelope unit-econ: $/1M tokens under 3 pricing configurations (pilot, tiered, committed).
- $/feature estimate and projected margin at your stated volumes.
- CAC payback scenarios assuming a 12–24 month contract and standard onboarding.

Attachment: CareStream_MA_plan_template.pdf (mutual action plan template)

Proposed next step: 30-min follow-up on Thursday to review the packet and align on a pilot. Please confirm availability.

Thanks —
Laura Bennett
Senior Solutions Manager, Redwood Inference

Hi Laura — thanks for the clear recap. Confirming numbers and adding a couple of data points you asked for: 

Confirmed:
- Target initial MAU (devices): 50,000 (we expect this to reach ~120k by month 6 if pilot performs well).
- Features per active device/day: average 3 (peak 5).
- Avg tokens per feature call: we see 100–150; 120 is a good baseline.

Clarifications:
- No large batch/async workloads planned in the pilot — strictly real-time mobile flows.
- Budget range for pilot phase: $5k–$12k/month. Over a committed 12–24 month contract we can scale to $20k–$60k/mo depending on unit pricing and SLA.
- Our internal finance team prefers a target $/1M tokens in the $350–$600 range for renewals. Lower if we can get predictable latency and caching options.

Attaching our rough usage/cost sheet: initial_cost_model.xlsx

Happy to do Thursday afternoon PST for the follow-up. Samantha

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-11T11:30:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Payback metrics & pricing qualification for CareStream — internal B/OE

Laura / Karthik — quick internal back-of-envelope after Samantha’s numbers. Sending this as internal-only so we can iterate before sending the consolidated response to CareStream.

Assumptions (pilot):
- MAU: 50k devices; sessions/day: 3; avg tokens/feature: 120 => monthly tokens = 50,000 * 3 * 120 * 30 ≈ 540,000,000 tokens (540M). Note: that’s total tokens for all calls; if our model returns ~50 tokens per response, we should account for both request/response direction — the 120 tokens estimate Samantha gave already accounts for round-trip, so leave as-is.
- Latency SLO: 300–500ms p50; higher SLO incurs premium kernel paths.

Redwood cost bands (estimate per 1M tokens):
- Unoptimized hosted (no cache, no quantization): $720 / 1M tokens
- Optimized baseline (batching + KV cache + quantized): $420 / 1M tokens
- Dedicated commit pricing (reserved capacity + aggressive quantization): $260 / 1M tokens (requires 12mo commit + 8 GPU pool)

Pilot economics (50k MAU baseline, 540M tokens/month):
- At $420 / 1M => monthly inference cost ≈ $226,800.
- At $260 / 1M => monthly inference cost ≈ $140,400.

Unit-econ per feature (per-call):
- Tokens per feature: 120 => per-call cost at $420/1M = (120 / 1,000,000) * 420 = $0.0504 (~$0.05).
- At $260/1M => $0.0312 (~$0.03).

Observations:
- Samantha’s stated budget ($5k–$12k/mo pilot) is far below cost at current volumes — indicates they likely intend to pilot with a small fraction of devices, or they expect lower per-device frequency. Need to validate pilot scope (percent of fleet).
- If they commit to a 12–24 month reserved contract we can get to the $260 band and approach their finance target, but that requires commit + higher utilization.
- CAC/payback: with a $0.05 per-feature cost and an ARPU per active device of ~ $2–$5/month (hypothetical), payback will be >12 months unless we layer usage fees in the product or charge per-device minimums.

Next internal asks:
1) Laura: confirm what % of the 50k devices they intend to include in the pilot (1%, 10%, 100%).
2) Karthik: can you draft a 2-tier pilot pricing (pilot trial + committed tier) with sample invoice-level numbers?

Attachment: redwood_unit_econ_snapshot.pdf

Thanks —
Marcus
Senior Product Ops, Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Payback metrics & pricing qualification for CareStream — next steps

Hi Samantha — thanks for the numbers and the sheet. I reviewed Marcus’s back-of-envelope and pulled together a short, actionable set of options below so your finance and product teams can pick a path.

Option A — Small pilot (recommended if you want low cost while validating product-market fit):
- Pilot scope: 1% of devices (500 devices), 3 sessions/day; est tokens ≈ 5.4M tokens/month.
- Price (pilot rate): $420 / 1M tokens => monthly inference cost ≈ $2,268.
- $/feature: ~ $0.050.
- Remarks: keeps spend inside your stated pilot budget band ($5k–$12k).

Option B — Staged ramp (preferred for realistic scale but cost control):
- Pilot: 10% of devices for 2 months, then ramp to 25%
- Effective blended price: assume optimization benefits => $350 / 1M tokens initially, moving to $300 with commit.
- Estimated mid-ramp monthly cost (25% of fleet): 135M tokens => at $350 => $47,250/mo.

Option C — Committed (best unit economics, requires contract):
- 12–24 month reserved capacity, target $260 / 1M tokens => at full 50k fleet (540M tokens) => $140k/mo.
- $/feature at $260 band: ~$0.031.

CAC payback (illustrative):
- If average revenue per device is $4/mo and gross margin target is 60% post-inference: at pilot scale, payback < 6 months; at full-scale without commit (high per-token price) payback > 12 months. We’ll include a table in the packet showing sensitivity to ARPU.

Recommended next steps:
1) Confirm pilot percent-of-fleet (pick Option A or B).
2) If CareStream is open to a 12mo commit, we’ll prepare a committed pricing proposal (Option C) and a draft SOW.
3) Schedule Thurs 2:30pm PST to review the unit-econ packet; I’ll bring the B/OE and Marcus/Karthik will be on for pricing specifics.

I’ve uploaded a one-page unit-econ summary and the mutual action plan draft to the HubSpot record. DocuSign-ready proposal link will follow once you confirm Option.
